atoms.text: In the USA, the first-past-the-post electoral system has resulted in a two-party system dominated by the Democratic and Republican parties. This because winner-takes-all-elections make it difficult for third parties to win seats because they rarely come in first. As a result, voters avoid supporting third parties since those votes are unlikely to lead to victory.

The Democratic Party is a center-left U.S. political party. It generally supports progressive taxation (higher taxes on high earners and corporations), expanded social programs, and stronger government regulation of markets to protect consumers, workers, and the environment. Socially, Democrats emphasize community and social responsibility. The party’s strongest regional support is in Metropolitan areas and densely populated areas along the two coasts.

The Republican Party is a center-right to right-wing U.S. political party. It generally favors lower taxes, especially on individuals and businesses, and reduced government regulation to promote free markets. Socially, Republicans tend to support traditional values, are often religiously influenced, and many oppose abortion and expanded LGBTQIA+ protections. The party’s strongest regional support is in the Midwest and rural areas across the country.
